1	"""Deterministic 2D grid A* planner.
2	
3	Public entry points: ``plan(width, height, blocked, start, goal, costs=None,
4	trace=False, dynamic_blocked=None, max_expanded=None, snapshot=False,
5	max_cost=None, allow_wait=False, dynamic_costs=None)``,
6	``plan_any(width, height, blocked,
7	start, goals, costs=None, trace=False, dynamic_blocked=None,
8	max_expanded=None, snapshot=False, max_cost=None, allow_wait=False,
9	dynamic_costs=None)``,
10	``plan_k(width, height, blocked, start, goal, k, costs=None,
11	dynamic_blocked=None, max_expanded=None, max_cost=None,
12	allow_wait=False)``,
13	``plan_batch(width, height, blocked, requests, costs=None, trace=False,
14	dynamic_blocked=None, max_expanded=None, snapshot=False,
15	max_cost=None, allow_wait=False)``,
16	``plan_multi_start(width, height, blocked, starts, goal, costs=None,
17	trace=False, dynamic_blocked=None, max_expanded=None, snapshot=False,
18	max_cost=None, allow_wait=False)``,
19	``replay(width, height, blocked, start, goal, path, costs=None,
20	dynamic_blocked=None, diagnose=False, allow_wait=False,
21	dynamic_costs=None)``,
22	``resume(checkpoint, max_expanded=None)``,
23	``distance_field(width, height, blocked, goal, costs=None, trace=False)``
24	and
25	``distance_field_any(width, height, blocked, goals, costs=None,
26	trace=False)``.
27	
28	Semantics:
29	- Four-neighborhood moves, Manhattan heuristic. Without ``costs`` each step
30	  has unit cost. With ``costs`` (a height-by-width matrix of positive
31	  integers, row-major: ``costs[y][x]``) entering a cell costs that cell's
32	  value; the start cell's cost is never counted, so ``cost`` is the sum of
33	  the costs of the cells entered along the path.
34	- Tie-breaking is fully specified and order-independent: compare f, then h,
35	  then the (x, y) coordinate in lexicographic order.
36	- ``expanded`` counts exactly the nodes popped from the priority queue and
37	  closed for the first time (the goal counts when reached; stale heap
38	  entries and duplicate closings do not).
39	- Returns ``{"path": [...], "cost": int, "expanded": int}`` on success and
40	  ``{"path": None, "cost": None, "expanded": int}`` when unreachable.
41	- When ``trace`` is true, both kinds of results additionally include
42	  ``expanded_nodes``: the list of coordinate tuples closed for the first
43	  time, in expansion order (includes the start, and the goal on success);
44	  ``expanded == len(expanded_nodes)``. The field is omitted entirely when
45	  ``trace`` is false or omitted.
46	
47	Search budget (``max_expanded``):
48	- ``max_expanded`` may be omitted or ``None``, which keeps every key,
49	  value, exception type and validation order of the default behavior
50	  untouched. Otherwise it must be a non-negative integer that is not a
51	  bool: other types raise ``TypeError`` and negative values raise
52	  ``ValueError``. These checks run after all existing grid, costs,
53	  ``trace`` and ``dynamic_blocked`` validation (including the frame-0
54	  check) and before the search starts.
55	- The budget counts closed nodes (exactly what ``expanded`` counts); once
56	  the limit is reached no further node is closed. When the budget is
57	  provided the result always carries an additional ``status`` field:
58	  ``"found"`` when the goal was closed within the limit (the usual
59	  ``path``/``cost`` are returned), ``"unreachable"`` when the candidates
60	  were exhausted without reaching the goal, and ``"budget_exhausted"``
61	  when live candidates remained but the budget stopped the search (then
62	  ``path``/``cost`` are ``None`` and ``expanded`` is the actual closed
63	  count, at most ``max_expanded``).
64	- The budget applies identically in static and dynamic mode and never
65	  changes expansion order, path choice, trace entries or determinism: a
66	  budgeted trace is a prefix of the unbudgeted one. With ``trace=True``
67	  only actually closed nodes are recorded, so a zero budget records
68	  nothing -- even when ``start == goal`` a zero budget returns
69	  ``budget_exhausted`` with ``expanded == 0``; the single-point success
70	  result requires at least one closed node (``max_expanded >= 1``).
71	- ``replay`` is unaffected: it keeps validating candidate paths only and
72	  accepts no budget parameter.
73	
74	Cost limit (``max_cost``):
75	- ``max_cost`` may be omitted or ``None``, which keeps every key, value,
76	  exception type and validation order of the previous behavior untouched.
77	  Otherwise it must be a non-negative integer that is not a bool: other
78	  types raise ``TypeError`` and negative values raise ``ValueError``. The
79	  check runs after all existing grid, costs, ``trace``, ``dynamic_blocked``,
80	  ``max_expanded`` and ``snapshot`` validation and before the search
81	  starts.
82	- The limit caps the accumulated entering-cell cost of a route, measured
83	  from the start (the start cell still costs 0 and each entered cell costs
84	  its ``costs`` value, or 1 without ``costs``). A candidate whose
85	  accumulated cost would exceed the limit is discarded; a candidate at
86	  exactly the limit still competes. The limit applies identically in
87	  static mode, dynamic mode and ``plan_any``, and never changes expansion
88	  order, tie-breaks, the minimum-cost choice, the multi-goal endpoint
89	  comparison or trace entries.
90	- When ``max_cost`` is provided the result always carries ``status``:
91	  ``"found"`` on success, and on failure ``"cost_exhausted"`` when at
92	  least one candidate was discarded for exceeding the limit, otherwise
93	  ``"unreachable"`` (``path``/``cost`` are ``None`` and ``expanded``
94	  counts the actually closed nodes). When ``max_expanded`` is also given,
95	  a budget stop still takes priority with ``"budget_exhausted"``.
96	  ``trace`` keeps recording only actually closed nodes, and the
97	  ``start == goal`` single-point zero-cost result and the zero-budget
98	  rules are unchanged.
99	- With ``snapshot=True`` the checkpoint records the ``max_cost`` value
100	  when one was provided (and no new field when it was not). ``resume``
101	  treats a checkpoint without the field as ``None``, validates a present
102	  field with the same rules (``TypeError`` for wrong types, ``ValueError``
103	  for negative values or a state inconsistent with the limit) before any
104	  searching, and a resumed search is equivalent to one uninterrupted call
105	  with the same limit. ``replay`` accepts no ``max_cost`` parameter.
106	
107	Waiting in place (``allow_wait``):
108	- ``plan``, ``plan_any``, ``plan_batch``, ``plan_multi_start``, ``plan_k``
109	  and ``replay`` accept a final optional boolean ``allow_wait`` that
110	  defaults to ``False``. ``False`` -- or an omitted, ``None`` or empty
111	  ``dynamic_blocked`` -- keeps every key, value, exception type,
112	  validation order, four-neighborhood move, no-repeated-coordinate rule
113	  and tie-break of the previous behavior untouched. A non-bool
114	  ``allow_wait`` raises ``TypeError`` after the ``dynamic_blocked``
115	  checks (the frame-0 check included) and before the budget and snapshot
116	  checks; every other exception type and order is unchanged.
117	- With ``allow_wait=True`` a route may stay in its current cell from
118	  time ``t`` to time ``t + 1`` provided the cell is not blocked at frame
119	  ``t + 1``. Waiting adds no entering-cell cost (``cost`` still sums
120	  only the cells entered by moves, and ``max_cost`` caps only those) and
121	  is only generated while ``t + 1`` lies within the provided frames:
122	  after the last frame the last frame is still reused for moves but no
123	  further waits are generated. Consecutive waits repeat the same
124	  coordinate in the path; once a cell is left it may never be
125	  re-entered. ``start == goal`` still yields only the single-point
126	  zero-cost route.
127	- The minimum-cost choice, the endpoint selection and the complete-path
128	  lexicographic tie-break follow the existing rules, with the priority
129	  still f, then h, then the coordinate, then the time and finally the
130	  complete path, so results never depend on obstacle-set or in-frame
131	  iteration order. Wait states count toward ``expanded`` one per closing
132	  and the trace records their ``(x, y, t)`` triples; ``max_expanded``
133	  truncates them like any other state and the ``status`` values and
134	  priorities are unchanged. ``plan_k``, ``plan_batch``, multi-goal and
135	  multi-start results follow the same waiting semantics, and a
136	  successful path verifies in ``replay`` with the same cost and step
137	  count, the waits included in ``steps``.
138	- ``replay`` with ``allow_wait=True`` accepts consecutive stays only
139	  within the provided dynamic frames; stays in static mode or without
140	  frames, stays after the final frame and non-consecutive revisits all
141	  return the usual invalid structure. With ``diagnose=True`` a stay
142	  after the final frame reports the dedicated error
143	  ``wait_after_final_frame``.
144	- A budget-exhausted checkpoint records ``allow_wait`` when it was true
145	  and ``resume`` of such a checkpoint is equivalent to one uninterrupted
146	  call with the same setting. Checkpoints written without the field
147	  restore it as ``False``; a present non-bool field raises ``TypeError``
148	  and a field inconsistent with the recorded internal state raises
149	  ``ValueError``.
150	
151	Dynamic obstacles (``dynamic_blocked``):
152	- ``dynamic_blocked`` may be omitted, ``None`` or an empty sequence, which
153	  leaves the static behavior above untouched. Otherwise it must be a
154	  sequence of frames; each frame is an iterable of grid coordinates that
155	  are blocked at that time frame. Frame 0 constrains ``start``; the
156	  coordinate at path index ``t`` must avoid both the static obstacles and
157	  frame ``t``, and frames beyond the last one reuse the last frame.
158	- Moves are still four-neighborhood only: no waiting in place and no
159	  repeated coordinates along the path. Because feasibility of a route
160	  depends on the coordinates it already visited, candidates that reach the
161	  same ``(x, y, t)`` through different coordinate histories are distinct
162	  states and are never merged: every route that satisfies the constraints
163	  can be explored. ``cost`` is still the sum of the costs of the cells
164	  entered; the start cell is never counted.
165	- The minimum-cost feasible route is returned. When total costs tie, the
166	  fixed priority is f, then h, then x, y, t, and candidates still tied are
167	  ordered lexicographically by their complete coordinate sequence, so the
168	  result never depends on the iteration order of the obstacle sets, the
169	  coordinates inside a frame, or the traversal order.
170	- In dynamic mode ``expanded_nodes`` records ``(x, y, t)`` triples in
171	  actual closing order and ``expanded`` counts closed space-time route
172	  states one per entry; a discarded candidate is never recorded. When the
173	  same ``(x, y, t)`` is closed through different histories, its triple
174	  appears once per closing in closing order, and ``expanded`` counts each
175	  such entry. On failure ``path``/``cost`` are ``None``.
176	- Validation: the outer value must be a sequence and every frame an
177	  iterable of coordinates; strings/bytes and non-two-integer coordinates
178	  raise ``TypeError``, out-of-bounds coordinates raise ``ValueError``,
179	  duplicates within a frame are merged, and a ``start`` blocked at frame 0
180	  raises ``ValueError``. All checks run before the search starts.
181	
182	Time-varying costs (``dynamic_costs``):
183	- ``plan``, ``plan_any`` and ``replay`` accept a final optional
184	  ``dynamic_costs=None`` parameter. Omitting it, passing ``None`` or an
185	  empty sequence keeps every result key, exception boundary, expansion
186	  order, path choice and the legacy ``costs`` semantics of the previous
187	  behavior untouched; every other entry point keeps its signature.
188	- Otherwise ``dynamic_costs`` must be a sequence of height-by-width
189	  matrices of positive integers, one matrix per time frame. An outer
190	  value or frame that is not an acceptable sequence, or a cell that is
191	  not a non-bool integer, raises ``TypeError``; a wrong row or column
192	  count, a non-positive cost, or providing both ``costs`` and
193	  ``dynamic_costs`` raises ``ValueError``. All checks run after every
194	  pre-existing validation and before the search starts.
195	- When enabled, entering a coordinate at path index ``t`` costs that
196	  cell's value in frame ``t``; the start cell is still never charged and
197	  frames beyond the last one reuse the last frame. Waiting follows the
198	  existing rules and never produces an entering-cell cost. The search
199	  returns the globally minimum total ``cost`` route under the static and
200	  dynamic obstacle constraints; equal costs are still arbitrated by the
201	  existing endpoint and complete-path lexicographic rules, and
202	  ``expanded``/``expanded_nodes`` count only actually closed space-time
203	  states: distinct histories are never merged and no out-of-bounds,
204	  blocked or illegally repeated nodes are generated.
205	- ``max_cost`` caps the dynamic accumulated cost with the usual
206	  ``cost_exhausted`` and budget-priority rules; ``plan_any``'s winning
207	  endpoint rules, the trace shape, the ``start == goal`` result and
208	  unreachable results are unchanged. ``replay`` recomputes ``cost``
209	  with the same frames, so a legal path matches the planning result;
210	  the diagnostic error types and the ``steps`` rule are unchanged.
211	- With ``snapshot=True`` the checkpoint records ``dynamic_costs`` as a
212	  JSON-serializable structure (the field is omitted when they were not
213	  provided) together with the waiting setting, the accumulated state and
214	  the cost limit when one was provided; a resumed search matches one
215	  uninterrupted call field by field, the next checkpoint included. A
216	  checkpoint whose ``dynamic_costs`` is corrupt raises ``TypeError`` or
217	  ``ValueError`` and never silently degrades.
218	
219	Multi-goal planning (``plan_any``):
220	- ``plan_any(width, height, blocked, start, goals, ...)`` accepts the same
221	  grid, blocked, start, costs, trace, dynamic_blocked and max_expanded
222	  arguments as ``plan``, plus a non-empty ``goals`` sequence of candidate
223	  endpoint coordinates. It returns one deterministic minimum-cost route to
224	  any of the candidates, in the same result structure as ``plan``; the
225	  path's last point is the winning endpoint.
226	- The grid, costs, trace, dynamic-blocked and budget checks run in
227	  ``plan``'s order with the same exception types; ``goals`` takes
228	  ``goal``'s position in that sequence. The outer value must be a
229	  sequence: strings, bytes, ``None`` and other non-sequences raise
230	  ``TypeError`` and an empty sequence raises ``ValueError``. Each endpoint
231	  follows the coordinate structure and integer rules (bad shape or
232	  coordinate types raise ``TypeError``); out-of-bounds coordinates and
233	  endpoints on static obstacles raise ``ValueError``. Repeated candidates
234	  merge, so the input ordering never changes any result.
235	- The search keeps four-neighborhood moves, no waiting, no revisits, the
236	  persistent last frame and the entering-cell cost accumulation. A
237	  candidate blocked by the dynamic frame at the time a particular route
238	  arrives is not rejected up front (its coordinate is statically valid);
239	  that arrival is simply infeasible for that route's time frame while
240	  other arrival times still compete.
241	- Total ``cost`` decides; ties compare the endpoint coordinate ``(x, y)``
242	  lexicographically, then the complete coordinate path lexicographically.
243	  As in dynamic ``plan``, routes reaching the same cell through different
244	  coordinate histories are distinct states and are never merged, so the
245	  traversal is a best-first walk of the feasible route tree; expansion
246	  order and the trace never depend on goal order, the blocked sets or
247	  in-frame iteration order. A budget never replaces an already determined
248	  better route with a worse one.
249	- When no endpoint is reachable, ``path`` and ``cost`` are ``None``. With a
250	  budget the ``status`` field follows the same ``"found"``,
251	  ``"unreachable"`` and ``"budget_exhausted"`` rules, and ``trace`` only
252	  records actually closed nodes: coordinate pairs in static mode and
253	  ``(x, y, t)`` triples in dynamic mode. A ``goals`` containing ``start``
254	  yields the single-point zero-cost route under the same start-equals-goal
255	  and zero-budget rules as ``plan``. A successful path verifies offline in
256	  ``replay`` when its last point is passed as ``goal``, with the same cost
257	  and step count.
258	
259	Top-k planning (``plan_k``):
260	- ``plan_k(width, height, blocked, start, goal, k, costs=None,
261	  dynamic_blocked=None, max_expanded=None, max_cost=None)`` returns
262	  several distinct feasible routes on the same grid in one call. It
263	  first performs exactly ``plan``'s shared validation for the
264	  dimensions, coordinates, static obstacles, positive integer cost
265	  matrix and dynamic frames (including the frame-0 start check), and
266	  only then checks ``k``: a non-bool positive integer is required,
267	  wrong types raise ``TypeError`` and non-positive values raise
268	  ``ValueError``. The optional ``max_expanded`` and ``max_cost``
269	  limits are checked after all of that (the ``k`` check included),
270	  still before the search starts, with the same non-negative,
271	  non-bool integer rules ``plan`` uses (other types raise
272	  ``TypeError``, negative values raise ``ValueError``). Every error is
273	  decided before the search starts, and ``plan_k`` accepts no
274	  ``trace`` or ``snapshot`` argument.
275	- The search keeps four-neighborhood moves, the zero start cost, the
276	  entering-cell cost accumulation, the persistent last frame, the ban on
277	  waiting in place and on repeated coordinates, and the static/frame
278	  feasibility rules. Routes that reach the same cell through different
279	  coordinate histories are distinct candidates and are never merged, in
280	  both static and dynamic mode, so different complete coordinate
281	  sequences always remain separate results.
282	- It returns ``{"paths": [...], "costs": [...], "expanded": int}``: at
283	  most ``k`` unique complete routes ordered by ascending total cost and,
284	  on ties, by the lexicographic order of the complete coordinate
285	  sequence; ``costs`` corresponds to ``paths`` entry by entry. The first
286	  entry is the route ``plan`` would return. When no route is feasible
287	  both lists are empty and ``expanded`` still reports the route
288	  candidates actually closed to determine the answer: one count per
289	  complete history, and never counting a candidate filtered at
290	  generation or left pending. The traversal stops the moment the k-th
291	  goal route has been closed, so a small k closes strictly fewer
292	  candidates than a larger one. ``start == goal`` yields only the
293	  single-point zero-cost route, with one expansion. Every returned route
294	  verifies offline in ``replay`` with the same cost and step count, in
295	  both static and dynamic mode; the result never depends on obstacle-set
296	  iteration order, in-frame coordinate order or the traversal order.
297	- ``max_cost`` caps a route's accumulated entering-cell cost exactly as
298	  in ``plan``: the start still costs 0, a candidate exactly at the
299	  limit still competes and a candidate whose accumulated cost would
300	  exceed it is discarded the moment it is generated. It never changes
301	  the tie-break between legal routes. ``max_expanded`` caps the number
302	  of complete route candidates actually closed (exactly what
303	  ``expanded`` counts); once the limit is reached no further candidate
304	  is closed, and the limit only ever truncates the traversal -- it can
305	  never replace an already determined higher-ranked route. When either
306	  limit is provided the result additionally carries ``status``:
307	  ``"found"`` when all ``k`` routes were closed or the search exhausted
308	  naturally with at least one route; ``"budget_exhausted"`` when fewer
309	  than ``k`` routes were found and the budget stopped the search while
310	  candidates were still pending (this wins when both limits fire);
311	  ``"cost_exhausted"`` when fewer than ``k`` routes were found, no
312	  budget stop occurred and at least one candidate was discarded for the
313	  cost limit; ``"unreachable"`` when no route exists with neither a
314	  budget stop nor a cost discard. The routes already closed (and their
315	  costs, in rank order) are still returned when a limit ends the search
316	  early, as empty lists when none were found, and ``expanded`` is the
317	  actual closed count. Omitting both limits keeps every legacy key and
318	  value exactly unchanged.
319	
320	Batch planning (``plan_batch``):
321	- ``plan_batch(width, height, blocked, requests, costs=None,
322	  trace=False, dynamic_blocked=None, max_expanded=None, snapshot=False,
323	  max_cost=None)`` answers several independent single-goal queries on
324	  one shared grid in a single call. It returns ``{"results": [...]}``
325	  with exactly the result ``plan`` would return for each query, in the
326	  order of ``requests``; duplicate requests are kept and each gets its
327	  own result.
328	- The shared arguments are validated with ``plan``'s rules and order,
329	  with ``requests`` taking the position of ``start``/``goal`` in that
330	  sequence. ``requests`` must be a non-empty sequence: ``None``,
331	  strings, bytes and other non-sequences raise ``TypeError`` and an
332	  empty sequence raises ``ValueError``. Each element must be a
333	  two-element sequence ``[start, goal]`` of grid coordinates: element
334	  shape or coordinate type failures raise ``TypeError``; out-of-bounds
335	  coordinates, endpoints on static obstacles and a start blocked at
336	  dynamic frame 0 raise ``ValueError``. Every check is decided before
337	  any search starts, so an invalid batch never returns partial results.
338	- Each query is an independent ``plan`` search over the shared grid:
339	  ``path``, ``cost`` and ``expanded`` are produced per request, and the
340	  ``max_expanded`` budget and the ``max_cost`` limit apply per query
341	  with no state shared across queries. ``trace``, ``status``,
342	  ``expanded_nodes``, ``checkpoint``, dynamic frames, ``start == goal``,
343	  unreachable and ``cost_exhausted`` results all follow ``plan``
344	  exactly, and a returned ``checkpoint`` can be handed to ``resume``
345	  directly. A successful path ends at its request's goal and verifies
346	  offline in ``replay`` with the same cost and step count. The result
347	  never depends on obstacle-set iteration order, in-frame coordinate
348	  order or the permutation of ``requests``.
349	
350	Multi-start planning (``plan_multi_start``):
351	- ``plan_multi_start(width, height, blocked, starts, goal, costs=None,
352	  trace=False, dynamic_blocked=None, max_expanded=None, snapshot=False,
353	  max_cost=None)`` plans from several candidate starts to one shared
354	  goal in a single call and returns one deterministic route, in exactly
355	  the result structure of ``plan``; the path begins at the winning start
356	  and ends at ``goal``. ``starts`` takes ``start``'s position in
357	  ``plan``'s validation sequence and every shared check keeps its order,
358	  exception type and message boundary.
359	- ``starts`` must be a non-empty sequence of grid coordinates: ``None``,
360	  strings, bytes and other non-sequences raise ``TypeError`` and an
361	  empty sequence raises ``ValueError``. Each start follows the
362	  coordinate structure and integer rules (bad shape or coordinate types
363	  raise ``TypeError``); out-of-bounds coordinates and starts on static
364	  obstacles raise ``ValueError``. Repeated starts merge and the tuple is
365	  sorted, so the input ordering never changes any result. A start
366	  blocked by dynamic frame 0 raises ``ValueError``; every check runs
367	  before the search starts.
368	- In static mode every start is a ``g == 0`` root and each coordinate is
369	  closed at most once: a cell keeps only its best known ``(cost, path)``
370	  pair (smallest accumulated entering-cell cost, then the
371	  lexicographically smallest complete coordinate sequence -- an ordering
372	  preserved under common extensions, so a dominated candidate can never
373	  win later). In dynamic mode the persistent last frame, the ban on
374	  waiting and on repeated coordinates apply, and routes reaching the
375	  same ``(x, y, t)`` through different coordinate histories are distinct
376	  states that are never merged.
377	- The winning route has the smallest total ``cost``; ties are decided by
378	  the lexicographic order of the complete coordinate path, so the result
379	  never depends on the input order of ``starts``. Expansion order is f,
380	  then h, then ``(x, y)`` (plus ``t`` in dynamic mode), and finally the
381	  complete path. ``cost`` counts only the cells entered (the winning
382	  start costs 0); ``expanded`` counts only closed candidates; when no
383	  route exists ``path`` and ``cost`` are ``None``.
384	- With ``trace=True`` static mode records the unique coordinate closing
385	  sequence and dynamic mode the ``(x, y, t)`` closing sequence, and
386	  ``expanded == len(expanded_nodes)``. A ``starts`` entry equal to
387	  ``goal`` yields the single-point zero-cost route under the same
388	  start-equals-goal and zero-budget rules as ``plan``.
389	- ``max_expanded`` and ``max_cost`` follow ``plan``'s ``status`` and
390	  budget-priority rules: a candidate whose accumulated cost would
391	  exceed ``max_cost`` is discarded without counting toward ``expanded``,
392	  and neither limit ever changes the unlimited route or the tie-breaks.
393	  With ``snapshot=True`` a budget stop returns a JSON-serializable
394	  checkpoint recording the sorted starts, the grid constraints, the
395	  dynamic frames, the cost limit when one was provided and the complete
396	  pending state; ``resume`` continues it with the cumulative-budget,
397	  no-double-counting and only-budget-exhausted-snapshots rules of the
398	  other planners, and invalid checkpoints follow ``resume``'s usual
399	  ``TypeError``/``ValueError`` boundaries.
400	
401	Snapshots and resumable planning (``snapshot`` and ``resume``):
402	- ``plan`` and ``plan_any`` accept a final ``snapshot=False`` option.
403	  Omitting it or passing ``False`` keeps every key, value, exception type,
404	  validation order, tie-break, unreachable result and trace of the
405	  previous behavior untouched. A non-bool ``snapshot`` raises
406	  ``TypeError`` after all existing checks (the ``max_expanded`` validation
407	  included) and before the search starts.
408	- With ``snapshot=True``, a search that stops because ``max_expanded``
409	  was reached (``status == "budget_exhausted"``) additionally returns
410	  ``checkpoint``: a fully JSON-serializable snapshot of the planner state.
411	  Results that already found the goal or proved it unreachable never
412	  carry the field.
413	- The checkpoint records the snapshot version, the planner kind, the
414	  normalized grid constraints (dimensions, obstacles, start, goal or
415	  candidate goals, costs, dynamic frames and the cost limit when one was
416	  provided), the closed-node count, the
417	  trace recorded so far and the complete pending-candidate state. Every
418	  set-derived list is stored sorted, so neither obstacle-set iteration
419	  order, goal order nor in-frame coordinate order influences the
420	  checkpoint's keys or values. A caller may store it as-is and hand it
421	  back to ``resume`` later.
422	- ``resume(checkpoint, max_expanded=None)`` continues the very same
423	  deterministic search described by the snapshot. ``max_expanded`` keeps
424	  its cumulative meaning: the total number of nodes that may be closed
425	  counted from the original start, so a limit not greater than the
426	  already closed count closes nothing more. The result is equivalent to
427	  one uninterrupted call with the same cumulative budget: ``path``,
428	  ``cost``, ``expanded``, ``status`` (present exactly when
429	  ``max_expanded`` is given) and ``expanded_nodes`` (always present in
430	  resume results; coordinate pairs in static mode, ``(x, y, t)`` triples
431	  in dynamic mode) all match, and repeated resumes never count an already
432	  closed node twice.
433	- When a resumed search reaches the budget again its result carries a
434	  fresh ``checkpoint`` that can be resumed in turn; ``found`` and
435	  ``unreachable`` results omit it. A successful resumed ``path`` verifies
436	  in ``replay`` with the same cost and step count.
437	- Validation: a checkpoint that is not an object, has missing required
438	  fields or wrongly typed fields raises ``TypeError``; an unsupported
439	  snapshot version or planner kind, grid constraints that violate the
440	  usual ``plan`` rules (obstacles, endpoints, costs, dynamic frames) or
441	  an internally inconsistent state raise ``ValueError``. Every check is
442	  decided before any searching, and ``resume``'s ``max_expanded`` follows
443	  the same non-negative-integer rules as ``plan``'s.
444	
445	Offline replay (``replay``):
446	- ``replay`` re-checks a saved candidate path without running any search;
447	  it never returns ``expanded`` or ``expanded_nodes``. It accepts the same
448	  grid arguments as ``plan`` (no ``trace``) plus ``path``.
449	- The grid arguments are validated with exactly the public ``plan``
450	  checks, and all of them run before the path is judged, so the same
451	  malformed grid inputs raise the same ``TypeError``/``ValueError``.
452	- ``path`` must be a non-empty sequence of grid coordinates; strings,
453	  bytes, ``None`` and other non-sequences raise ``TypeError``, as do
454	  elements that are not exactly two integers. Coordinates outside the
455	  grid raise ``ValueError``.
456	- A structurally valid but semantically invalid path does not raise: it
457	  returns ``{"valid": False, "cost": None, "steps": None}`` with no
458	  partial accumulation. Invalid means: not beginning at ``start``, not
459	  ending at ``goal``, visiting a static obstacle, visiting a cell blocked
460	  by frame ``t`` at path index ``t`` (the last frame persists for later
461	  indices; omitted/empty ``dynamic_blocked`` means static-only checks),
462	  non-four-neighbor adjacency, repeated coordinates, or extra points when
463	  ``start == goal``.
464	- A valid path returns ``{"valid": True, "cost": int, "steps": int}``
465	  where ``steps == len(path) - 1`` and ``cost`` is recomputed with the
466	  same entering-cell rule ``plan`` uses (sum of the costs of the cells
467	  entered; unit costs without ``costs``; the start cell is never
468	  counted), so it equals the cost ``plan`` assigns to that same path.
469	- ``diagnose`` defaults to false; omitting it or passing ``False`` keeps
470	  every key, value, exception type and validation order identical. A
471	  non-bool ``diagnose`` raises ``TypeError`` after all grid checks
472	  (including the frame-0 check) and before the path structure is
473	  inspected. With ``diagnose=True`` both results additionally carry
474	  ``error`` and ``error_index``: ``None``/``None`` for a valid path, and
475	  for an invalid one a single error code plus the zero-based index of
476	  the first offending element, with ``cost``/``steps`` still ``None``.
477	  The codes, in fixed precedence order, are ``start_mismatch`` (index
478	  0), ``goal_mismatch`` (index of the last element),
479	  ``start_goal_extra`` (index 1), ``repeated_coordinate`` (the second
480	  occurrence), ``non_adjacent`` (the later element of the pair),
481	  ``static_blocked`` and ``dynamic_blocked`` (the offending element);
482	  ties resolve to the earliest rule in this list and no partial cost is
483	  ever returned.
484	
485	Distance field (``distance_field``):
486	- ``distance_field(width, height, blocked, goal, costs=None,
487	  trace=False)`` is an offline analysis entry point for the static grid:
488	  it accepts only the dimensions, the static obstacles, a single goal and
489	  optionally ``costs`` and ``trace`` -- no start, no dynamic obstacles, no
490	  search budget, no cost limit and no snapshot option. The dimensions,
491	  goal coordinate, obstacle and costs checks (structure, integer types,
492	  bounds, duplicate merging, goal-on-obstacle) follow ``plan``'s public
493	  rules and order for those shared arguments and all run before the
494	  search starts; ``trace`` must be a bool (``TypeError`` otherwise).
495	- It returns ``{"distances": ..., "expanded": int}`` where ``distances``
496	  is a height-by-width matrix indexed ``distances[y][x]``: ``None`` for
497	  obstacles and for cells that cannot reach the goal, ``0`` for the goal
498	  itself, and for every other reachable cell the minimum sum of the
499	  entering-cell costs along a four-neighborhood route from that cell to
500	  the goal (unit steps without ``costs``; with ``costs`` each move adds
501	  the cost of the cell entered, exactly as ``plan`` accumulates ``cost``,
502	  so a reachable ``plan`` start yields the same value ``plan`` reports
503	  as ``cost``). No reachable distance is ever negative and the matrix
504	  always matches the grid dimensions; the result is JSON-serializable.
505	- ``expanded`` counts exactly the reachable cells determined and closed
506	  once each, the goal included. The closing order is fully specified:
507	  smallest current distance first, then the ``(x, y)`` coordinate in
508	  lexicographic order, so neither the obstacle-set iteration order nor
509	  the costs layout traversal influences the matrix, the count or the
510	  trace. With ``trace=True`` the result additionally carries
511	  ``expanded_nodes``, the coordinate pairs in that closing order, and
512	  ``expanded == len(expanded_nodes)``; the field is omitted entirely
513	  when ``trace`` is false or omitted.
514	
515	Multi-goal distance field (``distance_field_any``):
516	- ``distance_field_any(width, height, blocked, goals, costs=None,
517	  trace=False)`` is the multi-goal counterpart of ``distance_field``:
518	  one offline analysis returns the minimum-cost field to any of the
519	  candidate endpoints in a single pass. It accepts only the dimensions,
520	  the static obstacles, a non-empty ``goals`` sequence and optionally
521	  ``costs`` and ``trace`` -- no start, no dynamic obstacles, no search
522	  budget, no cost limit and no snapshot option, and it never produces a
523	  ``status`` field. The dimensions, obstacles, costs and trace checks
524	  follow ``distance_field``'s public rules and order, and ``goals`` is
525	  validated exactly like ``plan_any``'s: ``None``, strings, bytes and
526	  other non-sequences raise ``TypeError``, an empty sequence raises
527	  ``ValueError``, elements that are not exactly two non-bool integers
528	  raise ``TypeError``, and out-of-bounds coordinates or endpoints on
529	  static obstacles raise ``ValueError``. The goals checks occupy
530	  ``goal``'s position in ``distance_field``'s validation sequence,
531	  duplicates merge, and every check runs before the search starts, so
532	  the input permutation never changes any result.
533	- It returns ``{"distances": ..., "targets": ..., "expanded": int}``.
534	  ``distances`` is the same height-by-width matrix as
535	  ``distance_field``: ``None`` for obstacles and for cells that cannot
536	  reach any endpoint, ``0`` for every endpoint, and otherwise the
537	  minimum over the endpoints of the accumulated entering-cell cost
538	  along a four-neighborhood route (unit steps without ``costs``; with
539	  ``costs`` each move adds the cost of the cell entered, the start
540	  cell's own cost never counted, exactly as ``plan``/``plan_any`` and
541	  ``distance_field`` accumulate). A reachable ``plan_any`` start yields
542	  the same value ``plan_any`` reports as ``cost``.
543	- ``targets`` is a matrix of the same shape: a reachable cell records
544	  the coordinate tuple of the endpoint that wins it, every other
545	  position is ``None`` (obstacles and unreachable cells, exactly where
546	  ``distances`` is ``None``); endpoints record themselves. When several
547	  endpoints tie at the same minimum distance the winner is the endpoint
548	  with the lexicographically smallest ``(x, y)`` coordinate, so the
549	  choice never depends on goal order. The whole result is
550	  JSON-serializable.
551	- ``expanded`` counts every reachable cell closed for the first time,
552	  all endpoints included, exactly once each. The closing order is
553	  smallest distance first, then the ``(x, y)`` coordinate
554	  lexicographically. With ``trace=True`` the result additionally
555	  carries ``expanded_nodes`` -- the coordinate pairs in that order,
556	  ``expanded == len(expanded_nodes)`` -- and the key is omitted
557	  entirely when ``trace`` is false or omitted.
558	
559	Validation (all performed before the search starts):
560	- ``width``/``height`` must be positive integers.
561	- ``start``, ``goal`` and every entry of ``blocked`` must be grid
562	  coordinates: sequences of exactly two integers (tuples, lists, etc.),
563	  normalized to tuples.
564	- ``goals`` (``plan_any`` and ``distance_field_any``) must be a
565	  non-empty sequence of grid coordinates following the same rules,
566	  normalized, deduplicated and order-independent.
567	- ``requests`` (``plan_batch``) must be a non-empty sequence of
568	  two-element ``[start, goal]`` coordinate pairs following the same
569	  coordinate rules, with the input order and duplicates preserved.
570	- ``costs`` may be omitted or ``None`` (unit costs). Otherwise it must be a
571	  sequence of ``height`` rows, each a sequence of ``width`` positive
572	  integers; strings/bytes, non-integer cells and booleans are rejected.
573	- ``dynamic_costs`` (``plan``, ``plan_any`` and ``replay`` only) may be
574	  omitted, ``None`` or an empty sequence. Otherwise it must be a
575	  sequence of frames, each frame a height-by-width matrix following the
576	  ``costs`` rules per frame; providing both ``costs`` and
577	  ``dynamic_costs`` raises ``ValueError``.
578	- ``trace`` must be a bool; non-bool values raise ``TypeError``.
579	- Type or structure violations raise ``TypeError``; non-positive
580	  dimensions, out-of-bounds coordinates, endpoints on obstacles, wrong
581	  matrix shape, or non-positive cell costs raise ``ValueError``.
582	- Duplicate blocked cells are merged without changing the result.
583	"""

600	    return isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool)

603	def _validate_dimension(value, name):
604	    if not _is_int(value):
605	        raise TypeError(
606	            f"{name} must be an int, got {type(value).__name__}"
607	        )
608	    if value <= 0:

613	def _normalize_point(value, name):
614	    if isinstance(value, (str, bytes)) or not isinstance(value, Sequence):
615	        raise TypeError(
616	            f"{name} must be a sequence of two integers, "
617	            f"got {type(value).__name__}"
618	        )
619	    if len(value) != 2:
620	        raise TypeError(
621	            f"{name} must contain exactly two coordinates, got {len(value)}"
622	        )
623	    x, y = value[0], value[1]
624	    if not _is_int(x) or not _is_int(y):
625	        raise TypeError(f"{name} coordinates must be integers, got {value!r}")
626	    return (x, y)

629	def _check_bounds(point, width, height, name):
630	    x, y = point
631	    if not (0 <= x < width and 0 <= y < height):
632	        raise ValueError(
633	            f"{name} {point} is outside the {width}x{height} grid"

637	def _normalize_blocked(blocked, width, height):
638	    if isinstance(blocked, (str, bytes)) or not isinstance(blocked, Iterable):
639	        raise TypeError(
640	            f"blocked must be an iterable of grid coordinates, "
641	            f"got {type(blocked).__name__}"
642	        )
643	    cells = set()
644	    for index, item in enumerate(blocked):
645	        name = f"blocked[{index}]"
646	        point = _normalize_point(item, name)
647	        _check_bounds(point, width, height, name)
648	        cells.add(point)  # duplicates merge into one cell
649	    return cells

652	def _normalize_costs(costs, width, height):
653	    if costs is None:
654	        return None  # unit step cost
655	    if isinstance(costs, (str, bytes)) or not isinstance(costs, Sequence):
656	        raise TypeError(
657	            f"costs must be a height-by-width matrix of positive integers, "
658	            f"got {type(costs).__name__}"
659	        )
660	    if len(costs) != height:
661	        raise ValueError(
662	            f"costs must have exactly {height} rows, got {len(costs)}"
663	        )
664	    rows = []
665	    for y, row in enumerate(costs):
666	        if isinstance(row, (str, bytes)) or not isinstance(row, Sequence):
667	            raise TypeError(
668	                f"costs[{y}] must be a sequence of {width} positive "
669	                f"integers, got {type(row).__name__}"
670	            )
671	        if len(row) != width:
672	            raise ValueError(
673	                f"costs[{y}] must have exactly {width} cells, "
674	                f"got {len(row)}"
675	            )
676	        parsed = []
677	        for x, cell in enumerate(row):
678	            if not _is_int(cell):
679	                raise TypeError(
680	                    f"costs[{y}][{x}] must be an int, "
681	                    f"got {type(cell).__name__}"
682	                )
683	            if cell <= 0:
684	                raise ValueError(
685	                    f"costs[{y}][{x}] must be a positive integer, "
686	                    f"got {cell}"
687	                )
688	            parsed.append(cell)
689	        rows.append(tuple(parsed))
690	    return tuple(rows)

693	def _normalize_dynamic_costs(dynamic_costs, width, height):
694	    # ``dynamic_costs`` is the time-varying counterpart of ``costs``: a
695	    # sequence of height-by-width positive integer matrices, one per time
696	    # frame. ``None`` or an empty sequence disables it (equivalent to not
697	    # provided). The outer value and every frame must be sequences
698	    # (strings/bytes and other non-sequences raise ``TypeError``); a frame
699	    # with the wrong row count, a row with the wrong cell count, or a
700	    # non-positive cell cost raises ``ValueError``; a cell that is not a
701	    # non-bool integer raises ``TypeError``. All checks run before the
702	    # search starts.
703	    if dynamic_costs is None:
704	        return None  # time-varying costs disabled
705	    if isinstance(dynamic_costs, (str, bytes)) or not isinstance(
706	        dynamic_costs, Sequence
707	    ):
708	        raise TypeError(
709	            f"dynamic_costs must be a sequence of cost frames, "
710	            f"got {type(dynamic_costs).__name__}"
711	        )
712	    if len(dynamic_costs) == 0:
713	        return None  # no frames: equivalent to not provided
714	    frames = []
715	    for t, frame in enumerate(dynamic_costs):
716	        if isinstance(frame, (str, bytes)) or not isinstance(frame, Sequence):
717	            raise TypeError(
718	                f"dynamic_costs[{t}] must be a height-by-width matrix of "
719	                f"positive integers, got {type(frame).__name__}"
720	            )
721	        if len(frame) != height:
722	            raise ValueError(
723	                f"dynamic_costs[{t}] must have exactly {height} rows, "
724	                f"got {len(frame)}"
725	            )
726	        rows = []
727	        for y, row in enumerate(frame):
728	            if isinstance(row, (str, bytes)) or not isinstance(row, Sequence):
729	                raise TypeError(
730	                    f"dynamic_costs[{t}][{y}] must be a sequence of "
731	                    f"{width} positive integers, got {type(row).__name__}"
732	                )
733	            if len(row) != width:
734	                raise ValueError(
735	                    f"dynamic_costs[{t}][{y}] must have exactly {width} "
736	                    f"cells, got {len(row)}"
737	                )
738	            parsed = []
739	            for x, cell in enumerate(row):
740	                if not _is_int(cell):
741	                    raise TypeError(
742	                        f"dynamic_costs[{t}][{y}][{x}] must be an int, "
743	                        f"got {type(cell).__name__}"
744	                    )
745	                if cell <= 0:
746	                    raise ValueError(
747	                        f"dynamic_costs[{t}][{y}][{x}] must be a positive "
748	                        f"integer, got {cell}"
749	                    )
750	                parsed.append(cell)
751	            rows.append(tuple(parsed))
752	        frames.append(tuple(rows))
753	    return tuple(frames)

757	    if dynamic_blocked is None:
758	        return None  # dynamic mode disabled
759	    if isinstance(dynamic_blocked, (str, bytes)) or not isinstance(
760	        dynamic_blocked, Sequence
761	    ):
762	        raise TypeError(
763	            f"dynamic_blocked must be a sequence of frames, "
764	            f"got {type(dynamic_blocked).__name__}"
765	        )
766	    if len(dynamic_blocked) == 0:
767	        return None  # no frames: equivalent to not provided
768	    frames = []
769	    for t, frame in enumerate(dynamic_blocked):
770	        if isinstance(frame, (str, bytes)) or not isinstance(frame, Iterable):
771	            raise TypeError(
772	                f"dynamic_blocked[{t}] must be an iterable of grid "
773	                f"coordinates, got {type(frame).__name__}"
774	            )
775	        cells = set()
776	        for index, item in enumerate(frame):
777	            name = f"dynamic_blocked[{t}][{index}]"
778	            point = _normalize_point(item, name)
779	            _check_bounds(point, width, height, name)
780	            cells.add(point)  # duplicates merge into one cell
781	        frames.append(frozenset(cells))
782	    return frames

785	def _normalize_path(path, width, height):
786	    if (path is None or isinstance(path, (str, bytes))
787	            or not isinstance(path, Sequence)):
788	        raise TypeError(
789	            f"path must be a non-empty sequence of grid coordinates, "
790	            f"got {type(path).__name__}"
791	        )
792	    if len(path) == 0:
793	        raise TypeError("path must be a non-empty sequence of coordinates")
794	    points = []

803	def _normalize_goals(goals):
804	    # ``goals`` is the plan_any counterpart of ``plan``'s single ``goal``.
805	    # This performs the outer/structure pass in exactly the position where
806	    # ``plan`` structurally normalizes ``goal``: strings, bytes, ``None``
807	    # and other non-sequences are ``TypeError`` and an empty sequence is a
808	    # ``ValueError``; every element is normalized to a coordinate tuple
809	    # (element shape/coordinate type failures are ``TypeError``). Bounds and
810	    # obstacle checks follow in ``plan_any`` at the same relative positions
811	    # ``plan`` uses for its single goal. Duplicates merge and the tuple is
812	    # sorted so the input order never affects the result.
813	    if (goals is None or isinstance(goals, (str, bytes))
814	            or not isinstance(goals, Sequence)):
815	        raise TypeError(
816	            f"goals must be a non-empty sequence of grid coordinates, "
817	            f"got {type(goals).__name__}"
818	        )
819	    if len(goals) == 0:
820	        raise ValueError("goals must contain at least one candidate endpoint")
821	    points = set()
822	    for index, item in enumerate(goals):
823	        point = _normalize_point(item, f"goals[{index}]")
824	        points.add(point)
825	    return tuple(sorted(points))

959	    Cells are merged by coordinate: the best known ``g`` per cell is kept
960	    in ``g_score``, stale heap entries are skipped, and ``came_from``

962	    ``max_cost`` a candidate whose accumulated entering-cell cost would
963	    exceed the limit is discarded instead of queued, and the search

965	    failure can be reported as ``cost_exhausted``; the flag is part of
966	    the snapshot state so a resumed search stays equivalent to one
967	    uninterrupted call. With
968	    ``snapshot=True`` a budget stop additionally returns a checkpoint of
969	    the complete search state; ``state`` carries such a snapshot back in
970	    so ``resume`` continues the identical traversal. The snapshot needs

972	    recorded whenever ``trace`` or ``snapshot`` is true.

975	    def heuristic(point):

980	        if costs is None:

983

987	        # is never compared.
988	        h0 = heuristic(start)
989	        open_heap = [(h0, h0, start[0], start[1], start)]
990	        came_from = {}
991	        g_score = {start: 0}
992	        closed = set()
993	        expanded_nodes = [] if trace or snapshot else None
994	        cost_limited = False
995	    else:
996	        open_heap = state["open"]
997	        came_from = state["came_from"]
998	        g_score = state["g_score"]
999	        closed = state["closed"]
1000	        expanded_nodes = state["expanded_nodes"]
1001	        cost_limited = state["cost_limited"]

1003	    has_status = max_expanded is not None or max_cost is not None
1004	
1005	    while open_heap:
1006	        entry = heapq.heappop(open_heap)
1007	        current = entry[4]
1008	        if current in closed:
1009	            continue  # stale heap entry; already closed with its best g
1010	        if max_expanded is not None and len(closed) >= max_expanded:
1011	            # A live candidate remains but the budget is spent; close
1012	            # nothing more (this also covers start == goal with a zero
1013	            # budget: no node is closed and no start is fabricated). The
1014	            # popped candidate was already removed from the heap, so for a
1015	            # snapshot it is pushed back: the checkpoint must hold every
1016	            # still-live candidate for the search to resume exactly.

1089	    two routes reaching the same ``(x, y, t)`` with different histories

1091	    the larger accumulated cost can be the only one that remains
1092	    extendable). Each heap node therefore carries its complete path; the
